chunks: “Thunder is the sound of an angel, larger than a fly and smaller than a wasp. So it is fitting for the one who hears the sound of thunder to say: ‘Glory be to the One whom...’
‘the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels [also] out of fear of Him.’

key_terms.الرَّعْدَ: thunder, presented here as a sign connected to an angelic reality
key_terms.بِحَمْدِهِ: with His praise; in a state of praising Allah
key_terms.خِيفَتِهِ: fear of Him; reverent awe before Allah
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: glory be; an expression of tanzih and divine exaltation
key_terms.مَلَكٍ: an angel, whose sound is identified with thunder
key_terms.يُسَبِّحُ: glorifies; declares Allah's transcendence and praise

ai.seo_question: What should one say when hearing thunder in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be said upon hearing thunder, linking the natural phenomenon to the glorification of Allah. It also invokes a Qur'anic expression, presenting thunder as a sign of divine power and a moment for dhikr.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1498 - It is narrated:
"The thunder is the sound of an angel that is larger than a fly and smaller than a wasp. When one hears the sound of thunder, it is recommended to say,
'Glory be to the One whom the thunder praises with His praise and (so do) the angels out of fear of Him.'
